why: Expression cycle 2 (docs/v3/cycles/expression-2.md) lost 47 of its 84 round-0 points to class `skill`, with 8 of its 17 P2s. The v3 references (agent/skills/basalt-design/references, fca6840e) already teach the baseline, the colour budget, annotating the mark that matters, one tab stop and say-it-once. Builders still shipped without them, and every one reached the device in a repair round once a reviewer named it. Two text gaps steered builds wrong. encoding.md sends 'many rows with several attributes' to a DataTable, so c07 answered 'which cases changed sides' with a table (F1 1, F7 0). Nothing says that Lines takes no marks and so cannot dim, which cost c09, n06 and n01's speed chart. The rest is a missing check before stopping: label collisions, light-mode contrast, a header that pushes rows below the fold, a ring that clips text and transitions without reduced motion only show on a rendered page.

change: Within the skill line budgets: (1) Answer on the mark: the hero states the answer with its verb ('Runs out 13:52', not '13:52'), and the one mark the page is about carries a direct annotation at rest; a list hides no answer below a cut (expression-2.1, .15, .28, .38, .51, .62). (2) Baseline check: every headline figure names its target, prior period or limit as a signed delta or as geometry, including a limit that is only a colour rule today (.2, .39, .52). (3) Colour budget check: a status hue only marks a state that needs action, never a target rule, a 'live' band or a passing delta; the failed mark takes the status fill, not its category hue (.3, .17, .29, .40, .53). (4) Form: in encoding.md, a count of items that changed state, or a pass/fail per item, is one mark per item (a square per case) with the table holding the detail; a series that must dim on focus is CartesianChart marks, because Lines takes no marks; Bars dims through its own opacity; intervals on a time axis get a row (.14, .20, .24, .42, .50, .56, .64). (5) Finish of a seam-drawn form: a focused-item mark beside the container ring, the ring inset so it clears text, tabular numerals in the page's own markup, motion-safe on any transition, no off-ladder value, and no status token as text in a CSS module, which the lint does not reach (.10, .11, .13, .25, .31, .35, .37, .60). (6) Fixture honesty: the extreme reads true (no rounding or clamping it away), a zero fixture shows a cue, binned bars carry a unit caption, every section's skeleton holds the loaded height, and an empty state names the next step once (.4, .8, .45, .49, .54, .58). (7) At 390 the answer and the first rows sit above the fold (.12). (8) Anatomy: cards in one row align their heights, and a card's subtitle is never filler where facts belong (.21, .57). Put (1)-(3) and (5)-(8) into one checklist that step 5 of basalt-design and step 6 of basalt-charts run against the rendered page at 1800 and 390, light and dark, and a keyboard-focused frame.
